decisions.statement: A reading is read by four operations and no more operations.
One operation answers whether a path stands.
One operation answers the children a directory lists.
One operation answers the lines an entry file has.
One operation answers the body a file in the repository holds.
The first three take a path under the index, and the fourth a path under the repository.
A reading built over no repository answers no body.
A lay answers the body a change leaves at a path rather than the body on disk.
A path the change takes away answers no body.
A path the change does not carry answers the body beneath the lay.
An entry file is read at the first ask and one copy of it is held.
A directory is listed at the first ask and that listing is held for that reading.
No entry file is held in more than one copy.
An entry file unmoved since it was last read is answered from the copy held rather than read again.
An entry file is unmoved where its inode, its width and when it was written are as they were.
A writer lands an entry file by renaming one into place, so its inode moves.
A reading made later answers the entry file on disk rather than the copy held.
No copy held answers for a body written after that copy was read.
The copies held are bounded, and the ones asked for longest ago go first.
A reader takes that surface rather than reaching for the disk.
The surface that reader reads can be something other than the committed index.
A reading laid over another reading has only the entry files a change touches.
A lay carries the lines that came and the lines that went rather than whole files.
A touched file's lines are worked out at the first ask and held for that lay.
A lay merges what came into the lines already in order rather than sorting them again.
A reading laid over a laid reading is laid over the reading beneath that one.
The entry files of both are one set, and the later act's lines are the ones read.
No reading is reached through another reading laid over the same one.
An entry file emptied by the change does not stand.
A directory left with nothing standing under that directory does not list.
An index emptied of every entry stands where the reading beneath that index stands.
A directory with no emptied path is listed straight through.
An index not there yet is read as an index that is there and has nothing.
Nothing here writes.
A body is read whole rather than as lines, and is held in no copy.
Nothing here loads a body as a value.
A reading laid over another leaves that one answering as it did.
A lay is worked out from the acts laid rather than from the acts laid before.
A root is answered the index under that root itself.
A worktree is a root of its own, so a worktree is answered an index of its own.
A reading answers the directory that reading reads from.
A reading laid over another answers the directory the one beneath it reads from.
A reading answers its root by the directory, as that reading answers any path.
No reading asks whether the index that reading reads is whole.
Whether a path in the repository is a path under the index is answered here.

definition: the reads a reading answers, and one reading laid over another so a change is read unwritten
